title: OpenAI adds $500 Pro tier, nerfs existing $200 tier
content:
OpenAI adds $500(!) Pro subscription, nerfs its existing $200 tier
The company also announced a new version of its Sol model.
Announced during the company's DevDay event today, OpenAI's new Pro 500 plan offers OpenAI's highest usage allowance and comes with access to its new "Ultrafast" feature — it also costs $500 per month. At the end of 2024, OpenAI became the first AI lab to introduce a $200 Pro plan. Nearly every other provider, including Anthropic and Perplexity, later announced their own $200 tiers, so it's possible other competitors will follow suit.
"Ultrafast is our premium speed tier for workloads where speed matters most," the company explains. With the feature enabled, OpenAI's Codex and Work apps will generate up to 300 tokens per second, making them capable of writing code and carrying out other tasks faster. The Ultrafast speed tier is also available to API users.
At the same time, OpenAI is also making its existing $200 Pro plan less appealing. In Codex and Work, $200 Pro subscribers will see their included usage decrease from 20x of what the company offers to Plus users, down to 10x of that same allowance. In ChatGPT, meanwhile, GPT-6 Pro message caps will decrease from 200 to 100 per week. According to the company, existing subscribers will keep their current limits for a time, and will later receive a one-time credit to help them make the most of their new reduced allowances.
All Pro subscribers will get a single Dot, the name OpenAI is giving to its new personal AI agents. Additionally, any conversations you have with your Dot won't count toward your ChatGPT usage limit. The company is partnering with 16 companies, including Notion and Cognition, to let Plus and Pro customers run OpenAI models in those services by using the new "Sign in with ChatGPT" option. No need to firstset up an API key.
OpenAI today also announced GPT-6.1 Sol. The company says the new model offers nearly the same performance of its current frontier system, GPT-6.0 Astra, in areas like coding and computer use, while costing one fifth of the price. OpenAI claims the new model is also safer to use. "GPT-6.1 Sol is more transparent about its limitations and more reliable at respecting user intent and safety constraints," the company says. "In challenging evaluations, it shows lower failure rates than GPT-6 Sol on transparency about broken search tools, respecting explicit restrictions, and avoiding unauthorized outcomes during agentic tasks."
Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education users can start using GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex and Work starting today, with availability in ChatGPT to follow at a later date.

report.summary: OpenAI launched a $500 monthly Pro tier with Ultrafast speed while cutting usage limits on its existing $200 Pro plan and unveiling GPT-6.1 Sol.
report.background: OpenAI’s DevDay move extends a pricing experiment that began in late 2024, when it became the first major lab to launch a $200 monthly Pro subscription. Rivals including Anthropic and Perplexity soon copied the $200 tier, turning high-end consumer AI into a familiar market segment. As frontier models and agentic products consume more compute—especially for coding, computer use, and always-on agents—vendors are looking for ways to segment heavy users, fund inference costs, and monetize speed and reliability rather than just raw model access. At the same time, cheaper, more efficient models like GPT-6.1 Sol let OpenAI serve more users at lower cost per task. The $500 tier and reduced $200 limits reflect that dual strategy: premium pricing for the most demanding workloads, plus efficiency gains passed partly to developers.
key_points: OpenAI's new Pro 500 plan costs $500 per month and offers the highest usage allowance plus Ultrafast, a premium speed mode that lets Codex and Work generate up to 300 tokens per second. The feature is also available to API users, targeting latency-sensitive coding and agent workloads.

The existing $200 Pro tier is less generous. In Codex and Work, included usage drops from 20x Plus to 10x Plus. In ChatGPT, GPT-6 Pro message caps fall from 200 to 100 per week. Current subscribers keep old limits temporarily and later get a one-time credit.

Every Pro subscriber gets one Dot, OpenAI's new personal AI agent. Chats with Dot do not count against ChatGPT usage limits. OpenAI is also partnering with 16 companies, including Notion and Cognition, so Plus and Pro users can run OpenAI models in those services via 'Sign in with ChatGPT' without an API key.

OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Sol, a cheaper model that performs nearly as well as frontier GPT-6.0 Astra in coding and computer use while costing one fifth as much. OpenAI says Sol is safer, more transparent about limitations, better at respecting restrictions, and less likely to take unauthorized actions in agentic tasks.

GPT-6.1 Sol rolls out today for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Education users in Codex and Work, with ChatGPT availability to follow later. The launch pairs cost-efficient model serving with premium speed and agent access, sharpening OpenAI's tiered pricing strategy.
report.impact: For the AI industry, OpenAI is normalizing a $500 consumer/prosumer tier and making speed, usage, and agent access the new premium axes. Competitors that copied the $200 tier may face pressure to add higher-priced plans or usage-based pricing. For developers, Ultrafast API access is attractive for real-time coding assistants and agents, but teams must now model token budgets more carefully; GPT-6.1 Sol's lower cost may offset some increases. Regular users lose value on the $200 plan and face an upsell to $500, though the Dot agent and partner integrations add convenience. The bigger signal is that frontier AI is becoming a segmented utility: cheap models for scale, expensive tiers for guaranteed speed and capacity.
report.tools: To follow or test alternatives, watch OpenAI's Codex, Work, and API docs for Ultrafast quotas and GPT-6.1 Sol pricing. Open-source tools like LiteLLM can proxy multiple providers with budgets, fallbacks, and usage tracking; vLLM or Ollama support self-hosted inference. OpenRouter helps compare model prices and latency across vendors. For agent integrations, try Notion and Cognition's offerings once 'Sign in with ChatGPT' goes live, and compare Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Perplexity tiers.
